title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Outcome of a Review
content:
## Clause

A Dangerous Goods Acceptance review has three possible outcomes at any moment of handling: approved, rejected, or still under review. Which of them applies is settled in two stages.

**Whether the file can be decided.** That depends on the declaration file and the account alone: the shipper's signed initial declaration has to be on file, and the account has to reflect the charges that the file's declarations have given rise to. A file that falls short on any of these grounds keeps the status under review, and no decision is recorded on it.

**What the decision is.** A file that can be decided is approved when the goods fit their category and rejected when they do not. Nothing else enters into the choice between the two.

## Outcome grid

| File can be decided | Goods fit | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| no | any | under review, no decision recorded |
| yes | yes | approved |
| yes | no | rejected |

## Points of judgement

**The goods plainly fit, but the file cannot be decided.** The status stays under review; fit alone does not produce an approval.

**The file can be decided and one container test fails.** The review is decided as rejected.
